sourceRef: spec-item-surfaces.md (module 20, `item-surfaces`) + ssot-presentation.md 4.2/4.3 + ssot-inventory.md 5.9/534-541 + ssot-generation.md 855-862 + game-gui-principles.md GG-50/GG-26. Every number here is a PRESENTATION threshold -- how many rows a surface draws before it changes strategy, and how much of a 127-row catalog it shows. NONE of them meters the player: D26 puts drop volume, bag capacity and pacing out of this program's scope entirely, and the loot filter is the interface answer to review pressure, never the metering one.

collectionStrategy.note: GG-50: every collection declares its behaviour at 10, 100 and 1000. At or below renderAllThrough the armoury draws every row; above it and at or below virtualizeThrough it virtualizes; above virtualizeThrough it goes search-first. ssot-inventory.md:534-541 measured ~2,000 rolled rows as the point the FE needs virtualisation and search. NOT A CAP: nothing here refuses a row, and `RpgStore.InventoryCeiling` (20,000) is module 2's own structural abuse guard, which is a different thing and says so in its own comment. Raising these numbers changes only how the list is drawn.

compendium.note: ssot-presentation.md 4.3's four closed states. `oneAwayDistance` is the boundary between `one-away` (dimmed, atoms shown, the missing ingredient named) and `known-inactive` (dimmed, name only) -- the doc fixes it at `distance == 1`, and it is here so a playtest can widen the hint without a rebuild. `knownInactiveRowCap` bounds only the NAME-ONLY tail of a 127-row catalog; active and one-away rows are never dropped, so the cap can never hide a combination the player is about to earn. A DISPLAY bound on one list, not a limit on how many combinations may exist or fire.

lootFilter.note: D26 and spec-item-surfaces.md: `40/day` is I12 asking for A LOOT FILTER, an interface requirement, never a drop cap -- and I12's wall-clock axis is restated PER CONTENT EVENT, which is the axis the game actually has. `defaultHideBelowRarityOrdinal` starts at 0 (hide nothing) deliberately: ssot-generation.md:859-862 says 'no loot filter on day one', and which rung the 'salvage everything below X' button starts at is one of this module's named ASK-FIRST questions -- shipping a non-zero default would answer it silently. `reviewPressurePerContentEvent` (ssot-inventory.md: ~60 reviewed before players stop reading) and `inflowWatchPerContentEvent` (ssot-generation.md's 40 tripwire, re-axised) are WATCH numbers a surface may warn on. Nothing in this module reaches generation; crossing either number changes what is drawn, never what drops.

surfaceUnlocks.note: GG-44: complexity unlocks, and a locked surface SAYS WHAT UNLOCKS IT rather than being invisible or present-but-dead. information-architecture.md 7 fixes the Relics layer's own unlock at 'first container acquired'; the socket surfaces wait for a socketed item because a socket bench over an item with no sockets is present-but-dead. These are STATE keys, not a constant list -- the surface renders from what the player has. NOTE on `comparison`: the honest condition is 'a second candidate exists for a role you have filled', and the role half is not answerable today -- an armoury row's role lives on its BASE TYPE and module 6 shipped readers, not a table. So the key is deliberately the weaker, TRUE `second-container-owned` rather than a role-aware name the server would have to guess at. Tighten it the day module 6's table lands.
